c.tagline: The first city of the Americas — cobblestone Zona Colonial, a Caribbean Malecón, and merengue.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis are unmetered — agree the fare before getting in. App-based Uber and InDrive are widely used, cheaper, and give an upfront price; motoconcho (motorbike) taxis are common for short hops.

emergency.note: 911 is the unified national emergency line for police, fire, and ambulance across the Dominican Republic.

hood_landmark.Malecón / Bella Vista: Malecon Santo Domingo George Washington Avenue
hood_landmark.Zona Colonial: Zona Colonial Santo Domingo Calle Las Damas

avoid.reason: Caution in Cristo Rey, Capotillo and the colonial-zone fringes at night; petty crime/scams

hood_desc: The oldest European-founded city in the Americas and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a walkable grid of cobblestone streets around Calle El Conde and Parque Colón, home to the first cathedral of the New World, the Alcázar de Colón, and Calle Las Damas; the atmospheric first-timer base packed with cafes, bars, and colonial museums.

A leafy, centrally located older neighborhood of tree-lined streets and early-20th-century homes between the Colonial Zone and the Malecón, home to the National Palace, the Plaza de la Cultura museums, and the Palacio de Bellas Artes; quiet, cultural, and budget-friendly.

An upscale, modern district of glass high-rises, luxury hotels, fine dining, and designer shopping (Blue Mall and Ágora Mall nearby); the polished business-and-nightlife heart of the modern city, safe and walkable in parts.
An affluent, lively neighborhood next to Piantini filled with restaurants, rooftop bars, cafes, and shopping malls; a favorite for a dressier night out and modern comforts away from the tourist core.

The Caribbean waterfront along Avenida George Washington, a palm-lined boulevard of big hotels, casinos, monuments, and weekend open-air merengue; lively and scenic, though some stretches feel run-down, so stick to the hotel corridor.
lodging: Embassy Suites by Hilton Santo Domingo
Renaissance Santo Domingo Jaragua Hotel & Casino

water.note: Drink bottled water; even locals avoid the tap.

transit.hours: The Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM (extended on weekends), and the Teleférico keeps similar hours. Guaguas run all day but thin out after dark, so most visitors switch to Uber or InDrive at night.
transit.note: The two-line Metro and the Teleférico cable car are clean, cheap, and safe but don't reach the Colonial Zone or the Malecón directly; within the walkable Zona Colonial you go on foot, and Uber/InDrive fill the gaps.
transit.pay: The Metro and Teleférico share the rechargeable Tarjeta metro card, tapped at turnstiles; a single ride is about RD$20. OMSA buses take cash, and informal guaguas are paid in cash to the cobrador (roughly RD$25-40). Uber and InDrive charge in-app by cash or card.

bus: Caribe Tours & Metro Servicios Turísticos (intercity coaches)
ferry: Ferries del Caribe to San Juan, Puerto Rico (from the Santo Domingo port)
train: Santo Domingo Metro (urban rapid transit only; the country has no intercity passenger rail)

transit.m: Official airport taxi (fixed fare) to Zona Colonial (~35 min)
Uber or InDrive to the city where available (30-40 min)

tip.r: Restaurants add a 10% service charge plus 18% ITBIS tax; leaving an extra 5-10% for good service is customary. Round up for taxis.
